subject: Experiment readout draft (Q1 pricing) + meter caveats + proposal for next iteration
body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Experiment readout draft (Q1 pricing) + meter caveats + proposal for next iteration

Sharing the latest draft readout for the Q1 pricing/packaging experiments.

Attachments:
- 2026Q1_Pricing_Experiments_Readout_DRAFT_v5.pdf
- Metering_Caveats_for_Experiment_Analysis_2026-02-12.docx
- Next_Iteration_Plan_2026-02-12.xlsx

TL;DR
1) The directional results look consistent with what we expected (Variant B improves self-serve conversion; slight short-term GM pressure driven by model mix), BUT we have metering caveats that materially affect confidence for some segments.
2) Recommendation: we treat this as “draft directional,” then do one more iteration with pre/post meter-fix segmentation and updated exports before we lock guidance and sales messaging.

Key caveats (please read the 1-pager attachment; highlights below):
- Retry/fallback double-counting: Eng has a fix in flight (ref: PR-27463). Pre-fix windows will overstate billed tokens for streaming-heavy workloads with server-side retries.
- Missing/incorrect region dimension: impacted margin attribution and regional pricing comparisons (ref: PR-27541). This affects the GM overlay charts by region.
- Embeddings batching accounting: fix is in (ref: PR-27569) but historical windows are noisy for a small set of high-volume batched embedding users.

Practical implications for decision-making:
- Any “margin delta” we present needs an explicit tag: PRE-METER-FIX vs POST-METER-FIX.
- For Variant B, the conversion lift signal is strong enough that I’d keep running, but I’m not comfortable publishing final pricing guidance to the field until we rerun with the corrected meter outputs (or shadow-billing compare) and annotate the charts.

Proposed next iteration + timeline (aiming to align with Feb close + exec decision cadence):
- By Fri 2/13 EOD: Finance/FP&A confirms which meter fixes materially change rev rec / invoice preview assumptions (Rishi + Laura).
- Mon 2/16: refresh datasets with corrected dimensions where available; rerun readout with segmentation (Product).
- Tue 2/17: review v6 readout in a 30-min exec slot (Evelyn/Laura/Jordan).
- Wed 2/18: if approved, we finalize internal guidance and start Sales Enablement roll-out with explicit caveat language vetted by Legal (Michael).

Two specific asks:
1) Evelyn/Laura: are you OK with us keeping Variant B running through 2/18 while we clean up the analysis, assuming we add a guardrail on max credits/discount exceptions in the meantime?
2) Michael: can you skim the caveats doc and confirm what we can/can’t say externally about meter adjustments (esp. language around retries, caching, and “billed vs raw tokens”)?

Thanks — and happy to walk through live if helpful.

Nikhil
Director PM, Hosted API
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Experiment readout draft (Q1 pricing) + meter caveats + proposal for next iteration

Thanks Nikhil.

On (1): I’m ok keeping Variant B running through 2/18 *if*:
- We explicitly label any internal summaries as directional pending meter-fix segmentation.
- We do not change any invoice outcomes retroactively without Finance + Legal sign-off.
- We put a temporary cap on discretionary credits tied to the experiment window (Jordan—can you align RevOps / field managers on this today?).

Rishi + I will confirm by tomorrow which of the meter issues could move recognized usage in a way that matters for Feb invoice preview.

Laura
CFO, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Experiment readout draft (Q1 pricing) + meter caveats + proposal for next iteration

Works for me.

I’ll send a note to the RVPs + RevOps today:
- No bespoke “make-good” credits tied to experiment exposure without Finance approval.
- Any customer questions about token counting/retries get routed through the pricing FAQ draft (and we’ll update once Legal signs off).

Nikhil: for the eventual field version, we need a crisp one-liner for the common objection: “Are you double charging retries / does streaming inflate tokens?” — even if the answer is “no, and here’s the definition.”

Jordan
CRO, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Experiment readout draft (Q1 pricing) + meter caveats + proposal for next iteration

+1 to Laura’s constraints.

Nikhil, thanks for flagging the meter overlap clearly — we’ve been burned before by “clean” charts with unspoken instrumentation changes.

Decision-wise:
- Keep Variant B running through 2/18, but I want the v6 readout to include (a) the segmented view and (b) a short section titled “What we believe is real vs what is uncertain.”
- Please add one slide/page explicitly stating what changes once the meter fixes are in (e.g., billed tokens vs raw tokens visibility, cache attribution, etc.). This will be important for the sales narrative.

Michael: please advise on the externally-safe wording; I prefer we keep it factual and avoid implying past invoices were incorrect until Finance completes recon.

Evelyn
CPO, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 2:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Experiment readout draft (Q1 pricing) + meter caveats + proposal for next iteration

Skimmed the caveats doc.

Guidance for external language (until recon is complete):
- We can say we are “improving transparency and consistency of usage reporting” and “hardening meters to reduce edge-case discrepancies.”
- Avoid statements like “we previously overbilled” or “incorrect invoices” unless/until we have a specific account-level conclusion and approved remediation plan.
- For retries/fallbacks: safe phrasing is “requests are billed once per successful response; we use idempotency and dedupe safeguards; in rare edge cases we may issue credits after investigation.”
- For caching: we can define what a cache hit means and whether cached tokens are billed (this should match the current product policy; please confirm with Finance before we publish).

Send me the final FAQ blurb you want sales to use on “billed vs raw tokens,” and I’ll redline it quickly.

Michael
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks all.

Actions I’m taking:
- Readout v6: add explicit PRE/POST meter-fix segmentation, plus a “real vs uncertain” section and a page on what changes (transparency, fields in usage exports).
- Sales objection one-liner draft (for Legal review):
  "We bill for tokens processed to produce your response. Streaming doesn’t change the underlying token count, and requests are intended to be billed once per successful completion; we also publish ‘billed tokens’ alongside raw usage to make attribution clear. If you suspect an anomaly (e.g., retries), we’ll investigate and correct via credit when warranted."
- Temporary guardrail reminder: no bespoke experiment credits without Finance approval (Jordan, thank you for pushing).

Rishi: once you confirm which segments materially impact the GM model, I’ll prioritize those cuts in the v6 readout.

Targeting to send v6 Monday afternoon for review ahead of the 2/17 slot.

Nikhil
